newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission report sees beef export subsidies to 2005.
newsitem.headline: Commission report sees beef export subsidies to 2005.

text.p: Beef exports from the European Union will continue to need subsidies to the year 2005 because prices will remain above those of other exporting countries, the European Commission said in a report obtained by Reuters.

"The projected price gap between the EU and other major exporters, although decreasing over the forecast period, would remain too big to allow unsubsidised EU exports," said the report by the European Commission Directorate General for Agriculture (DG VI)

In "Situation and Outlook - Beef Sector", due to be released on Wednesday, DG VI forecasts that EU beef stocks will increase to an estimated 1.5 million tonnes by 2005 because of world trade export limits.
Measures taken to reduce production because of the mad cow crisis and a gradual recovery in consumption will reduce stock levels before 2001 but they will then accumulate again, it said.

EU expenditure on beef due to the mad cow, or BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) crisis which began in 1996, will continue through 1997 and will take the cost of the beef sector to historically high levels, it adds.

The report puts the expenditure share of the beef sector in 1996 and 1997 at 18 percent of farm spending, or 7.5 billion ecus, with the cost of BSE-related expenditure at 1.4 billion ecus in 1996 and 2 billion ecus in 1997.

The report is the first of several long term sectoral studies to help Commission President Jacques Santer draw up later this year financial guidelines for 2000 onwards and detailed ideas for reforming the EU's Common Agriculture Policy.
The report follows an overview published last month on the long term prospects for the grains, milk and meat markets.
